Community Comes Together to Plant 3,000 Native Trees at Bray Head 
Wicklow County Council is pleased to announce the success of a major native tree planting event 
held at Bray Head on 8th February, where close to 200 volunteers came together to help restore 
biodiversity at this iconic coastal site. 
The event marked the beginning of the implementation of the County Wicklow Biodiversity Action 
Plan 2026 to 2031. The plan mirrors national policy and the forthcoming National Restoration Plan 
in seeking to increase native tree cover and deliver biodiversity enhancement and habitat creation 
on public land. Public participation is central to this work, ensuring that biodiversity action is 
community led as well as policy driven. 
Despite weeks of torrential rain leading up to the event, early showers eased and the sun broke 
through over Bray Head as individuals, families and community group members from across 
Wicklow and beyond arrived to take part. Young and old worked side by side, planting 3,000 native 
trees supplied as whips by Cullen’s Nursery and delivered early on the morning of the event. Soft 
ground made for easy digging and the entire planting was completed in just a few hours. 
Ireland has one of the lowest levels of native tree cover in Europe, at less than 2%, and while 
Wicklow is often thought of as a forested county, the vast majority of its forest cover is non-native. 
This makes features such as hedgerows critically important for biodiversity. Often described as 
linear woodlands, hedgerows provide food, shelter and safe movement routes for a wide range of 
species. In Wicklow, around a third of the county’s 9,000 kilometres of hedgerows are in poor 
condition, underlining the importance of restoration efforts such as this.

Housing Needs Assessment 2024 (SSHA 2024)

assessments of national housing need. It provides vital data to inform the ongoing development of housing

captures the total number of households qualified for social housing support across the county whose social 
housing need is not being met, in order to understand the level of need for such support. The social housing 
applications were reviewed from 1st November 2023 to 4
th November 2024. The data on the housing needs for

Under CAS, the Department is accepting applications for capital funding for the delivery,

Assessment criteria 
CAS funding operates in partnership with Local Authorities and Approved Housing Bodies.  
Local Authorities assess the specific need for CAS funded housing being cognisant of the 
actual housing need of the CAS groups identified in the latest Social Housing Assessment, 
consultations with suitable local inter-agency/co-ordination groups that deal with special 
needs, such as the housing and disability steering groups, national policies and guidelines, 
including the National Housing Strategy for Disabled People.

Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in 
danger of becoming homeless.  
There are 9 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is 
continuous transition by the clients to suitable alternative accommodation. 
A report is being undertaken at present to cost the refurbishment of the current rooms with a view to 
making them all ensuite. More details will be available over the coming months. 
 
Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam 
Road, Wicklow as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed 
units, and two 3-bed units. Eleven families have now transitioned or are in the process of transitioning 
to a permanent home and the resulting vacancies are in the process of being occupied with families 
experiencing or in danger of homelessness. 
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary 
Accommodation) with key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into 
Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term accommodation.   
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – San Remo, Bray 
San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number 
of emergency/cold weather initiative beds and Supported Temporary Accommodation Beds (STA). 
There is on site key working support linking in with clients.    
The Neighbourhood Liaison Committee is now operational and meets monthly.

Peter McVerry Trust has been appointed as the Housing First Programme Implementer for the Mid-

surpassed the targets identified in the programme. Housing First recognises that a stable home 
provides the basis for recovery in other areas.  
 
Properties will be provided by both Wicklow County Council and Peter McVerry Trust for the

Wicklow County Council has, to date, successfully accommodated 18 clients under Housing First.  
Other clients proposed for Housing First have been assessed by the team and are availing of key 
support work pending finalisation of sourcing of accommodation. The main issue facing this 
programme is the availability of 1-bed units in suitable locations with easy access to required services.

Social Farming 
Social farming is an outcome focused, support placement for people, with a farmer, on a farm using 
the natural assets of the people, the place, the activities and the community to support a person 
achieve some of their own chosen goals.  There are currently three Social Farms based in County 
Wicklow which are based near Tinahely Arklow and Aughrim.  In February 2026, a service level 
agreement has been signed with Social Farming Ireland to roll out this project under the Healthy 
Ireland Fund.  For this initiative in Wicklow, partners will include care providers such as HSE Mental 
Health Services, Sunbeam, Rehabcare, Camphill, KARE and National Learning Network to give 
opportunities for support to participants on farms.

Croí Cónaithe (Towns, Cities and Rural) – Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant  
The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is a payment you can get if you are turning a vacant house or building into 
your permanent home or a rental property.  The grant applies to qualifying vacant properties in cities, towns, villages and 
rural parts of the country. 
There are 2 types of Grants available: 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant of up to €50,000 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant including the Derelict Property top up grant of up €70,000 
To qualify for the top up of €20,000, an independent report prepared by a Structural Engineer, along with a copy of their 
Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.

Residential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) 
 
Work progressed on the development of an Experience Builder web map to host the Annual Draft Map 2027 under the 
Residential Zoned Land Tax process. The application is being prepared for publication on the Wicklow County Council 
RZLT webpage to support public consultation and transparency. The map has been configured to present zoning 
information clearly and accessibly for members of the public and stakeholders.  
 
Bray & North Wicklow Area Partnership – County Wicklow Food Environment Map 
 
• 
Ongoing collaboration took place with Bray & North Wicklow Area Partnership in relation to the County Wicklow 
Food Environment Map project. Two mapping outputs are being progressed: a Research & Development Map 
and a public-facing interacticve map presenting background data in an accessible format. Enhancements were 
made to the web map, including the addition of bus routes and stops and improved user interaction tools. Further 
engagement is planned with project stakeholders, including the Healthy Ireland Wicklow team, to support the next 
phase of development. 
 
Planning & Environmental Data Support 
 
• 
Spatial data processing was undertaken to support Forward Planning, including land contour outputs and National 
Tree Map data extraction for Bray, Enniskerry and Kilmacanogue. Tree crown, polygon and point datasets were 
prepared to assist with evidence-based plan preparation. Support was also provided to the Environment section, 
including updates to buffers on a Nutrient Management Plan and completion of the associated ETL process. In 
addition, SEAI Building Energy Rating data was integrated into the Environment GIS Viewer to enhance internal 
access to environmental datasets.

groups and preparation of specific widgets for deployment.  These improvements contribute to a more reliable 
and user-friendly GIS environment across departments.
